title: Per-handler persistence wiring silently skipped whole transports
description: Persistence (WAL + replication) is wired call-site by call-site in the REST and envelope handlers. The RESP3 and SynapRPC dispatchers were written later and call the core stores directly (`kv_store.set(...)` then reply), so every non-transactional write over the native transports was neither logged nor replicated: the only persistence call under crates/synap-server/src/protocol/ was log_transaction in EXEC. The same per-site wiring also produced D-08 (REST and envelope APPEND/SETRANGE logged `log_kv_set(key, vec![], None)`). Neither a multi-agent review nor the transport tests caught it, because the tests check replies and never restart the server or read a replica. Rules: (1) when a cross-cutting concern (persistence, authorization, notifications, tenancy) is wired per handler, list every transport's dispatcher and grep each one for the concern before trusting it; `grep -rn persistence crates/synap-server/src/protocol/` returning only EXEC was the whole proof; (2) route the concern through one shared path that every transport must call; (3) parity tests must restart from the WAL and compare a replica, not just assert the reply.
whenToUse: Adding a transport, adding a cross-cutting concern, or reviewing durability/authorization claims across REST, envelope, RESP3, SynapRPC, MCP and UMICP.
whenNotToUse: A concern implemented inside the core store itself, which every transport reaches by construction.
